competences: The learner identifies key facts about district political and civic heads.
The learner explains the roles of district leaders using the sourced local-government materials.
languageCompetence: Learners read, write and pronounce: leader, councillor, district, local government, speaker, civic and political.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review district heads and identify their responsibilities.
By the end of the lesson learners should be able to answer original source questions about district leadership.
priorKnowledge: Learners finished the first lesson on district political and civic heads.
materials: P4 SST school reference notes on district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the preceding lesson on district leadership and asks "State any three roles played by the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) in the district.". They use the pupils' answers to connect earlier material to district political and civic heads — part b.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous Social Studies period, answer the opening question and identify leaders within their local council.

steps.stage: Development: Remember the district political and civic heads
steps.content: The political head of the district is Chairperson LC V. A mayor heads the municipality politically. Chairperson LC III heads a sub-county. The RDC represents the president in the district. The RDC is appointed by the president. The CAO heads district civil servants. The district speaker chairs council meetings. Civic leaders are appointed to provide social services.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Remember the district political and civic heads", including "The political head of the district is Chairperson LC V. A mayor heads the municipality politically." They explain the roles and ask "Name the district officials who are in charge of the following;" to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: State any three roles played by the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) in the district. | Name the district officials who are in charge of the following; | How does CAO attain leadership powers? | State any one role played by the district speaker.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original sourced questions, beginning with "State any three roles played by the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) in the district." and "Name the district officials who are in charge of the following;". They supervise learners' written responses and check their answers against the leadership notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, consult the facts in their notes and correct inaccurate answers after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher evaluates learning using "How does CAO attain leadership powers?" and "State any one role played by the district speaker.". They recap the source-grounded points and assign the remaining revision question for later practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one important district-leadership duty and correct their work in their books.

assessment: Check written and oral responses to "State any three roles played by the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) in the district.", "Name the district officials who are in charge of the following;", and "How does CAO attain leadership powers?" and mark against the source material.
homework: Complete the sourced question "State any one role played by the district speaker." in the Social Studies book.
